newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors demand death for "Filipino" spy.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors demand death for "Filipino" spy.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday demanded the death sentence for a North Korean charged with spying for Pyongyang while posing as a Filipino professor, a prosecutor said.

Mohamad Ali Kanso of Seoul's Dankook University, who is in fact North Korean Chung Su-il, was arrested at a Seoul hotel in July when he tried to fax information to a North Korean agent based in Beijing.
Chung admitted to being a North Korean agent, and to sending information on South Korea's military and political situation to the communist North via third countries over the past decade.
"The prosecution demands the death sentence in order to prevent a serious threat to national security, which is linked directly with people's lives," the prosecutor said.
The prosecutor quoted Chung as saying in court, "I apologise for endangering the well-being of the people (of South Korea) by engaging in an act of spying."
Chung, an official of the external information research department of North Korea's ruling Workers' Party, changed his name to fake his identity.

He earned a masters' degree in Lebanon before obtaining Philippine citizenship in 1984 by using forged documents. He came to South Korea later that year, attended a language institute and became a professor in 1990.
South Korea, which is technically at war with North Korea since their 1950-53 conflict ended with a truce rather than a peace agreement, bans all unauthorised contacts with Pyongyang.
